title: THE BLOOD OF JESUS
mv: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.
mvp: “In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.” Ephesians 1:7
assignment: List five (5) situations in a believer’s life where the power of the blood of Jesus can be declared or applied (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Blood is the vital fluid that circulates through the body, delivering oxygen and nutrients to cells and removing waste products. It is the core aspect of life. There are four components of blood: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. The Bible makes us understand that blood is the centre of life (Leviticus 17:11). The blood of Jesus symbolises the ultimate sacrifice and fulfilment of God's covenant. The blood of Jesus represents cleansing, covenant and the foundation of the Christian life (Hebrews 9:14-15).

As believers in Christ, we are forgiven of our sins by the blood of Jesus. We have been freed from the stain, shame, guilt, and consequence of sin (Hebrews 9:22; 1 John 1:7-9). Jesus’ shed blood paid the price necessary to redeem us (Hebrews 9:12; Ephesians 1:7). Jesus took the wrath we deserved on Him when He died, shed His blood and declared us justified (Romans 5:9). Sin separated us from God, the shed blood of Jesus reconciled us back to God (Colossians 1:20). We are washed in the blood of Jesus, consecrated, and set apart by God to be used as holy vessels (Hebrews 13:12). Those who believe in Jesus and place their faith in His finished work on the cross receive eternal life (John 3:36). We can boldly come into God’s presence at any time because of the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 10:19; Ephesians 2:13). Jesus came as the fulfilment of the law (Romans 10:4). By His death, He brought the New Covenant into effect. He shed His blood to guarantee the “better promises” of the New Covenant to all who believe in Him. (Matthew 26:28; Hebrews 8:6). We are healed by His blood (Isaiah 53:5; 1 Peter 2:24). We are victorious. The events of the Passover during the Exodus from Egypt were a foreshadowing of the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ on the cross (Exodus 12:13; Revelation 12:11).

i: Salvation: This is a major prerequisite (John 1:12). The blood of Jesus only works for those who belong to Him. You must repent, believe in Jesus, and accept Him as your Lord and Saviour before you can partake of His blood (Ephesians 1:7).
Obedience: You must be ready to obey God through His word (Isaiah 59:1-2; Romans 6:16-18).

Confession and Testimony: This is about declaring faith in Christ, confessing what His blood has done in your life, and testifying about your salvation and redemption (Romans 10:9-10; Revelation 12:11).

b.x: Victorious Christians are bold and unashamed to declare the name of Jesus Christ and the power in His blood.
